questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why money demand falls in hyperinflation
questions.stem: In a nurse's handover, Nurse Ada notes that during hyperinflation patients spend wages immediately because holding cash loses value fast, so money demand

options.text: falls because the opportunity cost of holding money soars
stays unchanged because nominal income still equals spending
options.misconception: names "stays unchanged because nominal income still equals spending" where the rule requires "falls because the opportunity cost of holding money soars"

options.text: rises as people hoard cash to hedge against rising prices
options.misconception: confuses money demand with hoarding behavior

options.text: rises because velocity of money decreases sharply
options.misconception: confuses "rises because velocity of money decreases sharply" with the correct "falls because the opportunity cost of holding money soars"

questions.explanation: Hyperinflation raises the cost of holding money, so real balances shrink and money demand falls. The tempting idea that people hoard cash ignores the inflation tax on balances.
questions.hint: Think about the cost of holding cash when prices explode.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.topic: From an open market purchase to money
questions.stem: Nurse Wendy's handover asks how an open market purchase ultimately raises the money supply

answer.exemplar: The central bank buys bonds, crediting bank reserves; banks lend excess reserves, and through the multiplier the broader money supply expands.

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this from an open market purchase to money item is: Reserves multiply through lending. That is why "The central bank buys bonds, crediting bank reserves; banks lend excess reserves, and through the multiplier the broader money supply expands" is the answer.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Movement along a short run Phillips curve
questions.stem: In a nurse's handover, Nurse Xavier notes unemployment falls; along the short-run Phillips curve

options.misconception: names "inflation is unchanged" where the rule requires "inflation rises"

questions.explanation: Lower unemployment raises inflation along the curve. Falling or unchanged inflation misstate the tradeoff.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Core inflation from the headline figure
questions.stem: Nurse Zoe's handover asks why policymakers focus on core inflation

answer.exemplar: Core inflation strips volatile food and energy prices, giving a clearer signal of underlying inflation trends and helping policy avoid overreacting to temporary shocks.

questions.explanation: For a core inflation from the headline figure question like this, the governing rule is: Core strips volatile items. Applying it gives "Core inflation strips volatile food and energy prices, giving a clearer signal of underlying inflation trends and helping policy avoid overreacting to temporary shocks" as the answer.
